verses.zh: 约瑟在左右站着的人面前情不自禁，吩咐一声说：「人都要离开我出去！」约瑟和弟兄们相认的时候并没有一人站在他面前。
verses.en: Joseph was no longer able to control himself before all his attendants,[NOTE:1] so he cried out, “Make everyone go out from my presence!” No one remained[NOTE:2] with Joseph when he made himself known to his brothers.
notes: Heb “all the ones standing beside him.”
Heb “stood.”
verses.commentary:
45:1 "Then Joseph could not control himself" This is a VERB (BDB 407, KB 410,
negated Qal PERFECT and a Hithpael INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, BDB 67,
KB 80), which is used of Joseph in Gen. 43:31, where he was able to get control of his emotions. Here he
wept so loudly (cf. Gen. 45:2) that everyone heard him weeping!

▣ "everyone go out from me" The command (BDB 422, KB 425, Hiphil IMPERATIVE),
possibly spoken in Egyptian, is directed to all of Joseph's servants (even his special steward). He is left
with only his eleven brothers.

▣ "when Joseph made himself known to his brothers" What a moment this must have been! Joseph
was emotional and they became emotional (cf. Gen. 45:3).

verses.zh: 他就放声大哭；埃及人和法老家中的人都听见了。
verses.en: He wept loudly;[NOTE:1] the Egyptians heard it and Pharaoh’s household heard about it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and he gave his voice in weeping,” meaning that Joseph could not restrain himself and wept out loud.
Heb “and the Egyptians heard and the household of Pharaoh heard.” Presumably in the latter case this was by means of a report.
verses.commentary:
45:2 "He wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard it and the household of Pharaoh heard
of it" Joseph had sent all his Egyptian servants out of the room. This was either

- so as not to embarrass his brothers

- so as not to show such great emotion in this personal matter before the Egyptians

However, the Oriental practice of loud wailing was heard by the servants who were close enough
to respond if Joseph had called them. Apparently, Joseph was a very loved man in Egypt and his servants
were personally concerned about him or were concerned about his expertise and governmental administration
being lost, therefore, they reported to Pharaoh what they had heard.

verses.zh: 约瑟对他弟兄们说：「我是约瑟。我的父亲还在吗？」他弟兄不能回答，因为在他面前都惊惶。
verses.en: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?” His brothers could not answer him because they were dumbfounded before him.
verses.commentary:
45:3 "I am Joseph" This is an exclamation with no VERB. It is supposition that he
spoke in Hebrew, but because it seems obvious to assume that his brothers did not speak Egyptian and that
there was no translator present, maybe Joseph shocked them by speaking to them in their native tongue and
making such a dramatic statement (cf. Gen. 45:4).

▣ "Is my father still alive" Some commentators have doubted the veracity of this verse
because in Gen. 43:27 Joseph asked the same question. However, it seems possible that the term (BDB 311,
cf. 1 Sam. 25:6) can mean more than simply physical life. Apparently he was asking about his father's
well-being, which we learn from later verses, had not been the same since the supposed death of Joseph
(cf. Gen. 45:27).

▣ "they were dismayed" This is a strong VERB (BDB 96, KB 111, Niphal
PERFECT, cf. Jdg. 20:41; 1 Sam. 28:21; 2 Sam. 4:1; Job 21:6; 23:15; Ps. 6:3; 30:8; 48:6;
83:17; 90:7; 104:29; Isa. 13:8; 21:3; Ezek. 7:27).

verses.zh: 约瑟又对他弟兄们说：「请你们近前来。」他们就近前来。他说：「我是你们的兄弟约瑟，就是你们所卖到埃及的。
verses.en: Joseph said to his brothers, “Come closer to me,” so they came near. Then he said, “I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.

verses.zh: 现在，不要因为把我卖到这里自忧自恨。这是　神差我在你们以先来，为要保全生命。
verses.en: Now, do not be upset and do not be angry with yourselves because you sold me here,[NOTE:1] for God sent me[NOTE:2] ahead of you to preserve life!
notes: Heb “let there not be anger in your eyes.”

You sold me here, for God sent me. The tension remains as to how the brothers’ wickedness and God’s intentions work together. Clearly God is able to transform the actions of wickedness to bring about some gracious end. But this is saying more than that; it is saying that from the beginning it was God who sent Joseph here. Although harmonization of these ideas remains humanly impossible, the divine intention is what should be the focus. Only that will enable reconciliation.
verses.commentary:
45:5 "Now do not be grieved or angry with yourselves, because you sold me here" The term "grieved"
(BDB 780, KB 864, Niphal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense) in the
Niphal stem is used in 1 Sam. 20:3,34; 2 Sam. 19:2 and Neh. 8:10,11. The basic meaning is "hurt,"
"pain," or "grieve."

The term "angry" is the term "burn" (BDB 354, KB 351, Qal JUSSIVE,
cf. Gen. 31:36; 39:19; Exod. 32:11).

Joseph is about to make one of the most astonishing faith statements found anywhere in
the Bible. This verse is the theological purpose of the Joseph account! In the midst of abuse and treachery
he was able to see the hand of God (Elohim) by faith. Verses 5-9 form one of the strongest affirmations
of the goodness and presence of God even amidst the struggles and problems of life.

Just an added comment on this powerful, wonderful text. My question has always been, "Does
God act in these ways only toward the covenant family?"It is obvious that God does whatever is necessary
to support the family of Abraham (cf. Romans 9-11), but what about ordinary believers? Is His love for
eternity (i.e., redemption) or for time and eternity? Is He with us in the same way? This world is an
evil, rebellious place (see The Goodness of God by John William Wenham). Believers suffer; believers are
persecuted; believers are killed! From the NT it seems true that God is with us and for us even amidst
circumstances that are unexplainable (see The Christian's Secrets of a Happy Life, by Hannah
Whithall Smith). It is a faith presupposition and a Scriptural revelation that believers are precious to
God! Life is a mystery, but the unseen (yet not unknown) hand of God is with us moment by moment. Our peace
must rest in Him, His Word, His Son, not in circumstances (cf. 1 Cor. 10:13; 13:8-13). We are the family
of Abraham (cf. Rom. 2:28-29; 9:6; Gal. 3:7,9,29; 6:16; Phil. 3:3)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL
REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 现在这地的饥荒已经二年了，还有五年不能耕种，不能收成。
verses.en: For these past two years there has been famine in[NOTE:1] the land and for five more years there will be neither plowing nor harvesting.
notes: Heb “the famine [has been] in the midst of.”
verses.commentary:
45:6 "For the famine has been in the land these two years, and there are still five years in
which there will be neither plowing or harvesting" This goes back to the revelation through Pharaoh's
dream that there would be seven severe years of famine.

verses.zh: 神差我在你们以先来，为要给你们存留余种在世上，又要大施拯救，保全你们的生命。
verses.en: God sent me[NOTE:1] ahead of you to preserve you[NOTE:2] on the earth and to save your lives[NOTE:3] by a great deliverance.
notes: God sent me. The repetition of this theme that God sent Joseph is reminiscent of commission narratives in which the leader could announce that God sent him (e.g., Exod 3:15).
Heb “to make you a remnant.” The verb, followed here by the preposition ל (lamed), means “to make.”
The infinitive gives a second purpose for God’s action.
verses.commentary:
45:7 Joseph's statement in Gen. 45:7, referring to the remnant (BDB 984) being preserved, relates
to his activity, not to the later theological use of the term "remnant" which refers to the believing,
faithful portion of the Hebrew people.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, THREE SENSES

▣

NASB, NKJV, NJB, Peshitta
"by a great deliverance"

NRSV
"many survivors"

TEV
"descendants survive"

LXX
"a great remnant (posterity)"

JPSOA
"an extradorinary deliverance"

This is literally the NOUN "escape" (BDB 812, cf. Jer. 25:35) and the
ADJECTIVE "great" (BDB 152). Joseph's aid to his family, by being raised to leadership in
Egypt, is described as a great deliverance engineered by YHWH (cf. Gen. 45:5,8; 50:20).

verses.zh: 这样看来，差我到这里来的不是你们，乃是　神。他又使我如法老的父，作他全家的主，并埃及全地的宰相。
verses.en: So now, it is not you who sent me here, but God. He has made me an adviser[NOTE:1] to Pharaoh, lord over all his household, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
notes: Heb “a father.” The term is used here figuratively of one who gives advice, as a father would to his children.
verses.commentary:
45:8 "and He has made me" The theological problem related to the doctrine of predestination is not
that God knows and effects human actions (as well as physical events), but to what extent is He responsible
(duplicitous) for human sin? Theologians (Strong, Systematic Theology, 2nd ed. pp. 423-425;
Erickson, Christian Theology, 2nd ed. pp. 424-426) have offered several theories which show God's
involvement in, but not initiation of, sinful acts (cf. James 1:14; 1 John 2:16).

- He can prevent an act (cf. Gen. 20:16)

- He can permit an act (cf. Ps. 81:12-13; Rom. 1:24,26,28)

- He can direct an act (cf. Gen. 37:21-22; 45:5,7,8; 50:20)

- He can limit an act (cf. 1 Cor. 10:13)

SPECIAL TOPIC: PREDESTINATION
(CALVINISM) Versus HUMAN FREE WILL (ARMINIANISM)

▣ "a father to Pharaoh and a lord of all his household and ruler over all the land of Egypt" This
seems to be a threefold description of Joseph's job assignment in Egypt.

- He had a unique relationship with Pharaoh. This has become an archaeologically documented title
as far back as 3000 B.C. It seems to refer to the position of Grand Vizier.

- "Lord of all his household" seems to be a reference to the management of Pharaoh's personal
property (cf. Gen. 41:40; 47:20-26).

- "Ruler over all the land of Egypt" seems to express his relationship in governmental administration
(cf. Gen. 41:41, 48-49, 55-56; 42:6-7).

Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, vol. 1, p. 49, and IVP Bible Background Commentary,
p. 74, shows how the term "father" came to be used as a title for one of Pharaoh's chief advisors. Fathers
were the principal teachers of children after they had reached a certain age of maturity, before this it was
the mother's task. In the spiritual realm, priests took the term "father" to describe themselves (Hebrew
wisdom teachers in Proverbs also took this title, as did priests in Jdg. 17:10; 18:19).

verses.zh: 你们要赶紧上到我父亲那里，对他说：『你儿子约瑟这样说：　神使我作全埃及的主，请你下到我这里来，不要耽延。
verses.en: Now go up to my father quickly[NOTE:1] and tell him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says: “God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me; do not delay!
notes: Heb “hurry and go up.”
verses.commentary:
45:9 Joseph addresses his brothers with several commands.

- hurry, BDB 554, KB 553, Piel IMPERATIVE, cf. Gen. 45:13

- go up, BDB 748, KB 828, Qal IMPERATIVE

- come down, BDB 432, KB 434, Qal IMPERATIVE

- do not delay, BDB 763, KB 840, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

verses.zh: 你和你的儿子孙子，连牛群羊群，并一切所有的，都可以住在歌珊地，与我相近。
verses.en: You will live[NOTE:1] in the land of Goshen, and you will be near me—you, your children, your grandchildren, your flocks, your herds, and everything you have.
notes: The perfect verbal form with vav consecutive here expresses instruction.
verses.commentary:
45:10 "You shall live in the land of Goshen" It is uncertain from the following verses whether this
refers to an announcement on behalf of Joseph (cf. Gen. 46:31) or simply logic as to where shepherds lived.
The land of Goshen (BDB 177) is located on the upper eastern side of the Nile, close to the land of Canaan.
It is later called the land of Rameses (cf. Gen. 47:6,11). It was the livestock-producing area of Egypt
(cf. Gen. 46:32-34).

▣ "and you shall be near me" This verse is often used as an evidence for the Pharaohs whom
Joseph served being part of the "Shepherd Kings," or Hyksos, who conquered Egypt by means of the compound
bow and horse drawn chariot. They ruled Egypt from 1720 to 1580 B.C. We know that they were
Semitic in origin and, therefore, it may have been easier for another Semite, such as Joseph, to rise in
their ranks. Throughout Egyptian history, Semitic people have held important places in government. The
capital of the Hyksos empire was located in Tanis or Zoan (cf. Ps. 78:12, 43). This is very close to the
land of Goshen. However, the later native Egyptian Pharaohs had their capital 400 miles south in the city
of Thebes. The dating of Joseph's administration in Egypt is still uncertain and this cannot be used as
conclusive evidence.

verses.zh: 我要在那里奉养你；因为还有五年的饥荒，免得你和你的眷属，并一切所有的，都败落了。』
verses.en: I will provide you with food[NOTE:1] there because there will be five more years of famine. Otherwise you would become poor—you, your household, and everyone who belongs to you.”’
notes: The verb כּוּל (kul) in the Pilpel stem means “to nourish, to support, to sustain.” As in 1 Kgs 20:27, it here means “to supply with food.”

verses.zh: 况且你们的眼和我兄弟便雅悯的眼都看见是我亲口对你们说话。
verses.en: You and my brother Benjamin can certainly see with your own eyes that I really am the one who speaks to you.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “And, look, your eyes see and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that my mouth is the one speaking to you.”
verses.commentary:
45:12 "Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see, that it is my mouth which
is speaking to you" The exact meaning of each of these phrases is somewhat uncertain (probably he is
not using an interpreter), but the overall thrust is easy to ascertain. Benjamin was uniquely related to
Joseph because they were both sons of Rachel. The phrase "my mouth" seems to be used as an idiom for
authority (cf. Gen. 45:21 and the interpretation of Rashi).

▣ "Benjamin" Rachel originally named him "son of my sorrow" (BDB 121) because she died while
giving him birth (cf. Gen. 35:18). However, Jacob changed his name to "the son of my right hand" (BDB 122).
Because of Jacob's unique love for Rachel, both Joseph and Benjamin were very special to him.

verses.zh: 你们也要将我在埃及一切的荣耀和你们所看见的事都告诉我父亲，又要赶紧地将我父亲搬到我这里来。」
verses.en: So tell[NOTE:1] my father about all my honor in Egypt and about everything you have seen. But bring my father down here quickly!”[NOTE:2]
notes: The perfect verbal form with the vav consecutive here expresses instruction.
Heb “and hurry and bring down my father to here.”
verses.commentary:
45:13 "all my splendor" This is the Hebrew word kabod (BDB 458). Its basic meaning (BDB 458 II)
is "heavy" (cf. Gen. 41:31, NASB, "severe"; Exod. 4:10, "heavy of tongue").

It came to be used of that which is valuable. Note the following usages.

- riches, Gen. 31:1; Isa. 10:3; 61:6

- splendor/success, Gen. 45:13

- beauty, Isa. 35:2

- severe famine, Gen. 12:10; 41:13; 43:1; 47:4,13

- honor, Num. 24:11

- much, Gen. 50:10,11 (i.e., mourning)

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (OT)

verses.zh: 于是约瑟伏在他兄弟便雅悯的颈项上哭，便雅悯也在他的颈项上哭。
verses.en: Then he threw himself on the neck of his brother Benjamin and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
verses.commentary:
45:14 "Then he fell on his brother Benjamin's neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck" The excesses
of Jewish interpretation, even in a helpful commentator like Rashi, can be seen in this verse. They say that
Joseph wept because of the destruction of the tabernacle at Shiloh, which was in Joseph's later land
allotment (cf. Joshua). Benjamin wept because of the destruction of the temple, for Jerusalem which is
really located in the tribal allocation of Benjamin. This shows the tendency of Jewish exegesis to
completely remove the historical setting of the verse and apply it to any major event in the life
of Israel.

verses.zh: 他又与众弟兄亲嘴，抱着他们哭，随后他弟兄们就和他说话。
verses.en: He kissed all his brothers and wept over them. After this his brothers talked with him.

verses.zh: 这风声传到法老的宫里，说：「约瑟的弟兄们来了。」法老和他的臣仆都很喜欢。
verses.en: Now it was reported[NOTE:1] in the household of Pharaoh, “Joseph’s brothers have arrived.” It pleased[NOTE:2] Pharaoh and his servants.
notes: Heb “and the sound was heard.”
Heb “was good in the eyes of.”
verses.commentary:
45:16 The brothers have recovered from

- the shock of Joseph's revelation of himself to them

- the fear of God for what they did to Joseph

- the fear of Joseph himself

verses.zh: 法老对约瑟说：「你吩咐你的弟兄们说：『你们要这样行：把驮子抬在牲口上，起身往迦南地去。
verses.en: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Say to your brothers, ‘Do this: Load your animals and go[NOTE:1] to the land of Canaan!
notes: Heb “and go! Enter!”
verses.commentary:
45:17-20 This is Pharaoh's message to Joseph for his family.

- say to your brothers, Gen. 45:17, BDB 55, KB 65, Qal IMPERATIVE

- do this, Gen. 45:17, BDB 793 I, KB 889, Qal IMPERATIVE

- load your beasts, Gen. 45:17, BDB 381, KB 378, Qal IMPERATIVE (this
VERB is found only here in the OT)

- go to the land of Canaan, Gen. 45:17, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE

- come (not in NASB), Gen. 45:17, BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERATIVE

- take your father and your households, Gen. 45:18, BDB 542, KB 534, Qal IMPERATIVE

- come to me, Gen. 45:18, BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERATIVE

- I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, Gen. 45:18, BDB 678, KB 733, Qal COHORTATIVE

- you shall eat the fat of the land, Gen. 45:18, BDB 37, KB 46, Qal IMPERATIVE

- do this, Gen. 45:19, BDB 793 I, KB 889, Qal IMPERATIVE

- take wagons, Gen. 45:19, same VERB as #6

- bring your father (lit. carry), Gen. 45:19, BDB 669, KB 724, Qal PERFECT with
waw used in an IMPERATIVE sense

- come, Gen. 45:19, same VERB as #5 and #7, but a Qal PERFECT used in an
IMPERATIVE sense

- do not concern yourselves with your goods (lit. "let not your eye with regret upon your vessels," Gen. 45:20,
BDB 299, KB 298, Qal JUSSIVE; same idiom used in Deut. 7:16; 13:8; 19:13,31; 25:12

verses.zh: 将你们的父亲和你们的眷属都搬到我这里来，我要把埃及地的美物赐给你们，你们也要吃这地肥美的出产。
verses.en: Get your father and your households and come to me! Then I will give you[NOTE:1] the best land in Egypt and you will eat[NOTE:2] the best[NOTE:3] of the land.’
notes: After the imperatives in vv. 17-18a, the cohortative with vav indicates result.
After the cohortative the imperative with vav states the ultimate goal.
Heb “fat.”

verses.zh: 现在我吩咐你们要这样行：从埃及地带着车辆去，把你们的孩子和妻子，并你们的父亲都搬来。
verses.en: You are also commanded to say,[NOTE:1] ‘Do this: Take for yourselves wagons from the land of Egypt for your little ones and for your wives. Bring your father and come.
notes: The words “to say” have been supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 你们眼中不要爱惜你们的家具，因为埃及全地的美物都是你们的。』」
verses.en: Don’t worry[NOTE:1] about your belongings, for the best of all the land of Egypt will be yours.’”
notes: Heb “let not your eye regard.”

verses.zh: 以色列的儿子们就如此行。约瑟照着法老的吩咐给他们车辆和路上用的食物，
verses.en: So the sons of Israel did as he said.[NOTE:1] Joseph gave them wagons as Pharaoh had instructed,[NOTE:2] and he gave them provisions for the journey.
notes: Heb “and the sons of Israel did so.”
Heb “according to the mouth of Pharaoh.”
verses.commentary:
45:21 "wagons" This is an Egyptian loan word meaning "two-wheeled cart pulled by cattle" (BDB 722,
cf. 1 Sam. 6:7) and does not refer to the war-chariots (BDB 939, cf. Gen. 41:43) of Egypt. Carts were
common in Egypt because of the very flat terrain. They were rare, or possibly unknown, in the land of
Palestine because it has rough, hilly terrain. One reason for the Philistine's ability to control the
coastal shephelah was because of their use of iron chariots. However, Israel's early victories occurred
in the hill country where the chariots were unusable. These carts must have been a very unusual sight in
the land of Canaan.

verses.zh: 又给他们各人一套衣服，惟独给便雅悯三百银子，五套衣服；
verses.en: He gave sets of clothes to each one of them,[NOTE:1] but to Benjamin he gave 300 pieces of silver and five sets of clothes.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “to all of them he gave, to each one, changes of outer garments.”
Heb “changes of outer garments.”
verses.commentary:
45:22 "changes of garments" This possibly refers to ornamental clothing (i.e., Exod. 3:22; 12:35),
which was one of the sources of wealth in the ancient world. It could have been to properly attire his
brothers in their new cultural setting (Egypt's elite class, cf. Gen. 41:14). However, it may denote new
clothes, not special expensive ones (i.e., Ruth 3:3).

▣ "but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of garments"
Joseph, of all people, should have been aware of the problem that favoritism causes, yet the cultural
setting is such that he lavished attention on his full-blooded brother (cf. Gen. 43:34).

verses.zh: 送给他父亲公驴十匹，驮着埃及的美物，母驴十匹，驮着粮食与饼和菜，为他父亲路上用。
verses.en: To his father he sent the following:[NOTE:1] ten donkeys loaded with the best products of Egypt and ten female donkeys loaded with grain, food, and provisions for his father’s journey.
notes: Heb “according to this.”
verses.commentary:
45:23 Remember how Jacob had sent gifts to "the man" of Egypt in Gen. 43:11, so now Joseph returns
the cultural expectation.

- ten donkeys loaded with the best things (BDB 375 CONSTRUCT BDB 595)

- ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread

Wow! What Jacob must have thought when he saw all this coming down the road!

verses.zh: 于是约瑟打发他弟兄们回去，又对他们说：「你们不要在路上相争。」
verses.en: Then he sent his brothers on their way and they left. He said to them, “As you travel don’t be overcome with fear.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “do not be stirred up in the way.” The verb means “stir up.” Some understand the Hebrew verb רָגָז (ragaz, “to stir up”) as a reference to quarreling (see Prov 29:9, where it has this connotation), but in Exod 15:14 and other passages it means “to fear.” This might refer to a fear of robbers, but more likely it is an assuring word that they need not be fearful about returning to Egypt. They might have thought that once Jacob was in Egypt, Joseph would take his revenge on them.
verses.commentary:
45:24 "he said to them, 'Do not quarrel on the journey'" The VERB (BDB 919, KB 1182,
Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense, used only here in Genesis and
only twice more in the Pentateuch) can be interpreted as relating to

- assessing blame for their actions toward Joseph in Genesis 37 (Rashi)

- fear (cf. Exod. 15:14; Deut. 2:25) of returning with the whole family and Joseph taking revenge

- continuing thoughts about Benjamin getting more food (Gen. 43:34) and now more clothes and silver
pieces (Gen. 45:22)

He was reminding them in a subtle way that God Himself had directed the circumstances, not that
their acts were not sinful (cf. Gen. 42:21,28; 44:16), but that God had a larger purpose (cf. Gen. 45:5,7,8;
50:20; Acts 7:9). God uses even evil for His purposes (cf. Acts 2:23).

verses.zh: 他们从埃及上去，来到迦南地、他们的父亲雅各那里，
verses.en: So they went up from Egypt and came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and they entered the land of Canaan to their father.”

verses.zh: 告诉他说：「约瑟还在，并且作埃及全地的宰相。」雅各心里冰凉，因为不信他们。
verses.en: They told him, “Joseph is still alive and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt!” Jacob was stunned,[NOTE:1] for he did not believe them.
notes: Heb “and his heart was numb.” Jacob was stunned by the unbelievable news and was unable to respond.
verses.commentary:
45:26 "but he was stunned" This word originally meant "to grow numb by means of being cold"
(BDB 806, KB 916, Qal IMPERFECT with waw, cf. Ps. 77:2; Hab. 1:4). It is obvious that these
brothers had to confess to their father what they had done years earlier, although this is not specifically
mentioned in the text. It is interesting to note that Joseph's dreams finally come to reality. YHWH knows
and controls history! Predictive dreams and prophecies are strong evidence of the uniqueness of the Bible
and the character of God.

▣ "for he did not believe them" The VERB (BDB 52, KB 63) is a Hiphil
PERFECT. Jacob had also not believed them about Joseph's death (cf. Gen. 37:31-35). Jacob's
sons lied to him often and he sensed it!

verses.commentary:
45:27 "the spirit of the father revived" This seems to imply that since Joseph's supposed death, Jacob
was depressed and that he was not the man he had once been. Sometimes the death of a favored child can
devastate parents almost to the point of never being able to recover.

verses.zh: 以色列说：「罢了！罢了！我的儿子约瑟还在，趁我未死以先，我要去见他一面。」
verses.en: Then Israel said, “Enough! My son Joseph is still alive! I will go and see him before I die.”
verses.commentary:
45:28 It is interesting that in Gen. 45:27 the Patriarch is called "Jacob," which speaks of his old
life, while in Gen. 45:28 he is called by his new name "Israel." This is possibly

- because of his renewed attitude of faith toward God and God's promised covenant which is linked to Joseph

- because Jacob is about to make a decision which will affect the entire covenantal people

The name "Israel" has always been difficult to interpret. Some theories based on Gen. 32:28-29
are:

- "let El persist"

- "may El preserve"

- "ruling with El"

- "prince of God"

I do not think that the different names refer to different sources (i.e., J.E.D.P.)! Whatever
the correct etymology, this name became the special title of the people of God. After 922 B.C.
it refers only to the northern ten tribes. After the return from exile in 538 B.C it again
becomes the title of the entire people of God.

Jacob responds in four ways.

- it is enough, no VERB (BDB 912 I)

- my son Joseph is still alive, no VERB

- I will go, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal COHORTATIVE

- and see him, BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERFECT used in a
COHORTATIVE sense

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

BACKGROUND STUDY

- In Genesis 42-44 Joseph tested his brothers to see if their attitude of manipulation, particularly
toward the sons of Rachel, had changed. This was primarily shown through their actions related
to Benjamin.

- Genesis 45 and 46 deal with the closing section of Joseph's rise to supremacy and the fulfillment
of God's plan for the physical deliverance of Jacob and the covenant family during the seven
years of famine.

- Genesis 45:5-9 is strikingly relevant as we see God's hand so evident in the life of Joseph in
what would seem to be tragic circumstances. If we could only learn this truth in our lives, what
a difference it would make. Nothing just happens to God's children (See Hannah Whithall Smith's
The Christian's Secret of a Happy Life).
